implementation_notes: serde makes the projection a property of the serialized type: derive Serialize on a narrow view struct built from &Domain, or keep one type and stop fields from reaching the wire with #[serde(skip_serializing)] and value-dependent #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]. What replaces the classic filter object is the derive macro plus the field attributes - the omitted fields are absent from the output and rustc keeps the view type honest when the domain type changes. Walking a serde_json::Value/Map and removing keys by hand is still justified when the retained field set is data supplied at runtime (a field mask), and in protobuf/gRPC stacks prost-types models exactly that mask; the derive-based view should be preferred whenever the field set is known at compile time.
pitfalls: skip_serializing only affects the outbound direction: without skip_deserializing (or a separate input type) the field is still accepted when the same type is used to read messages, so the filtered type is not a filtered contract.
A view that borrows (&'a str) is tied to the source's lifetime - holding it across an await point or moving it into a spawned task forces a clone that copies more than the projection needs.

Filtering a serde_json::Value into another Value erases the types: every field becomes untrusted JSON again, and a rename in the source turns into a missing key at the receiver rather than a compile error.
#[serde(skip_serializing_if)] is evaluated per field at serialization time, so a hot path pays the predicate for every message; a narrow struct has no such cost.
